paper: Ketcheson et al., NodePy: A package for the analysis of numerical ODE solvers, JOSS 5(55), 2515 (2020)

open_questions.q: Is NodePy's Butcher-tree order-conditions verification correct on RK methods where the default numerical .order() returns 0 (as seen for SSP53), and how many other library methods silently exhibit this default-tolerance failure mode?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Table 4.1 footnote: SSP53 returns 0 at default numerical tolerance with a 'may be due to round-off' warning, and only recovers order 3 under mode='exact'. Only 11 methods were tested; the frequency of this false-zero across the full library was not measured.
next_steps: Enumerate every RK method NodePy ships (rk.loadRKM catalog) and run m.order() at default tolerance vs mode='exact'.
Report the fraction that differ and characterize which method families (SSP, low-storage, embedded pairs) are most affected.
File an upstream issue with reproducer if the false-zero rate is non-trivial.

open_questions.q: Do NodePy's computed SSP coefficients (radii of absolute monotonicity) agree with independently derived values from the SSP literature for methods NOT covered in Ketcheson's own papers, e.g. third-party low-storage or multistep-SSP constructions?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Table 4.2 verified 4 SSP methods (SSP22, SSP33, SSP53, SSP104) and 3 non-SSP methods, all authored/curated by Ketcheson-lineage work. Independent third-party SSP methods were not tested; the check is not blind to author overlap.
next_steps: Pick 3-5 SSP RK methods from external papers (e.g. Gottlieb-Shu, Spiteri-Ruuth, Higueras) whose SSP coefficient is published.
Load coefficients into NodePy via ExplicitRungeKuttaMethod(A, b) and call absolute_monotonicity_radius().
Report per-method agreement to the third-party published radius (relative tolerance).

open_questions.q: How faithfully does NodePy handle low-storage Runge-Kutta implementations (2N-storage, 3S* formulations), given that its object model is centered on full (A, b) Butcher tableaus?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md tests only classical full-tableau RK methods; the paper mentions low-storage support but we did not exercise it. It is unclear whether NodePy exposes the low-storage coefficient sets (a_i, b_i) or reconstructs them from the dense tableau, and whether analytical properties (order, SSP) computed via the dense form are consistent with the low-storage form's actual runtime behavior.
next_steps: Locate NodePy's low-storage class (if present) and load a canonical 2N-storage method (e.g. Williamson 3rd-order, CarpenterKennedy).
Verify that .order(), .absolute_monotonicity_radius(), and stability region computed from the low-storage form match those computed from the equivalent dense tableau.
Run an actual IVP integration using the low-storage recurrence and check convergence rate against the dense-form integrator.

open_questions.q: Does NodePy expose implicit Runge-Kutta methods (Gauss, Radau, Lobatto IIIC, DIRK families) as first-class objects with correct order, A-stability, L-stability, and B-stability diagnostics, and do those diagnostics match textbook values?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md tests only explicit RK methods (RK44, Heun33, SSP22/33/53/104, Merson43, Fehlberg45, DP5, CK5, BuRK65 — all explicit). Implicit-RK support and its A-/L-stability machinery are not exercised. The paper mentions implicit methods but our C1-C4 coverage is explicit-only.
next_steps: Load Gauss-2 (order 4), Radau IIA-3 (order 5), Lobatto IIIC-2 (order 2) via NodePy's implicit-RK loader.
Verify .order() matches textbook order and that stability_function() yields the correct rational R(z) (compare to closed-form Pade approximants).
Check A-stability boolean and L-stability boolean against Hairer-Wanner tables.

open_questions.q: Under what circumstances do NodePy's symbolic (sympy-backed) computations diverge from numeric (float) computations for the same RK property, and what is the practical performance/accuracy tradeoff?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Table 4.1 shows the symbolic (mode='exact') vs numeric path already diverges on SSP53 (0 vs 3). No systematic characterization was done of when to trust each mode, how much slower the symbolic path is, or whether symbolic mode itself is stable for large-stage methods (e.g. SSP104's 10 stages).
next_steps: Benchmark m.order() default-numeric vs mode='exact' wall-clock time across methods of 2..15 stages.
Identify methods where the two modes disagree and classify the cause (tolerance choice, rational vs float order-condition residual).
Draft a decision rule ('use exact if stages > N or if numeric returns 0') and validate it on the full method catalog.
